newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala extends deadline in electricity bidding.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala extends deadline in electricity bidding.

text.p: The deadline for companies to qualify as a bidder for Guatemala's electricity privatization was extended to June 19 from June 12, an official of the government-run electric company said on Thursday.
Seventeen companies remain in the preliminary competition to purchase two electric plants for $30 million, part of Guatemala's sweeping privatization program.
The qualification deadline was extended at the request of some of those firms, Fernando Garcia of the Guatemalan Electric Company (EEGSA), told Reuters.
The winning bid will be chosen on July 30.

The Guatemalan Electric Company is selling the thermoelectric plants, with a combined capacity of 80 megawatts, under the General Electricity Law passed by Congress in September, which demonopolizes electric production and allows new producers to sell electricity directly to consumers on the open market.
The winning bid will offer the best package in terms of price per killowatt hour and capacity. The $30 million purchase price is set.
